mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) reduces the discount rate for equity cash flows, leading to higher valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 5.0% signals a tightening labor market, which typically precedes stronger corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 5.0%, the S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, which typically leads to higher corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100) signals an economic contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate profits decline.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO < 100, the S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Positive quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 > 0) indicates a growing economy, which typically supports higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of quarters when GDPC1 is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index above 2.0% (CPIAUCSL > 2.0%) signals rising inflation, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as real rates rise.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.0%, the S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which typically leads to higher consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in PAYEMS and decrease in UNRATE fails to predict positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of elevated policy rates (FEDFUNDS > 1.0%), the S&P 500 typically experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days as higher borrowing costs weigh on corporate profits.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS > 1.0%, the S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.
